messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the coefficient of viscosity, the angular velocity, and the geometry of the pendulum. Pendulum models must include this damping term when the oscillations occur in a viscous fluid medium. Medium viscosity effects become particularly important at small amplitudes, where linear resistance dominates. Dominates in the regime of low Reynolds numbers, where the resistive torque is directly proportional to angular velocity. Velocity-dependent linear damping should be incorporated into the equation of motion for the physical pendulum. Pendulum simulations that ignore this term will overestimate the amplitude and period over many cycles. Cycles of oscillation in a fluid environment represent the standard scenario in which the viscous correction must be applied.
